audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 15, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal genealogical, textual, and political audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for idealized David memory, Maacah's queen-mother role, qadesh translation, religious reform, temple treasury diplomacy, siege and proxy war, compulsory labor, foot disease, assassination, dynastic massacre, and prophetic-fulfillment claims.

verses.restored: In eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.

familiar.text: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat reigned Abijam over Judah.

modern.text: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah,

original.text: וּבִשְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן נְבָ֑ט מָלַ֥ךְ אֲבִיָּ֖ם עַל יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

familiar.text: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.

modern.text: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

original.text: שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מַעֲכָ֖ה בַּת אֲבִישָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: He walked in all sins his father did before him, and his heart was not whole with YHWH his Divine like heart of David his ancestor.

familiar.text: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father.

modern.text: And Abijam walked in all the sins that his father before him had committed, and his heart was not as fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of David his forefather had been.

original.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל חַטֹּ֥אות אָבִ֖יו אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה לְפָנָ֑יו וְלֹא הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו כִּלְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Nevertheless, for David's sake YHWH his Divine gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising his son after him and establishing Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Nevertheless for David’s sake did the LORD his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem:

modern.text: Nevertheless, for the sake of David, the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and to make Jerusalem strong.

original.text: כִּ֚י לְמַ֣עַן דָּוִ֔ד נָתַן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהָ֥יו ל֛וֹ נִ֖יר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְהָקִ֤ים אֶת בְּנוֹ֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וּֽלְהַעֲמִ֖יד אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: For David did upright in eyes of YHWH and did not turn aside from anything commanded all days of his life, except in matter of Uriah the Hittite.

familiar.text: Because David did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

modern.text: For David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not turned aside from anything the LORD commanded all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

original.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֥ה דָוִ֛ד אֶת הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא סָ֞ר מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֗הוּ כֹּ֚ל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו רַ֕ק בִּדְבַ֖ר אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי

verses.restored: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all days of his life.

familiar.text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

modern.text: And there was war between the houses of Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijam’s life.

original.text: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֧ה בֵין רְחַבְעָ֛ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Abijam and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Abijam, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י אֲבִיָּם֙ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמִלְחָמָ֥ה הָיְתָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין אֲבִיָּ֖ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָֽם

verses.restored: Abijam lay with his ancestors, and they buried him in City of David. Asa his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Abijam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa reigned in his place. Asa Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 14:1–15; 2 Chronicles 15:8–19)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אֲבִיָּם֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: In twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign over Judah.

familiar.text: And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Asa over Judah.

modern.text: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Asa became king of Judah,

original.text: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֥ךְ אָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother/queen mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

familiar.text: And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.

modern.text: and he reigned in Jerusalem forty-one years. His grandmother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

original.text: וְאַרְבָּעִ֤ים וְאַחַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מַעֲכָ֖ה בַּת אֲבִישָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Asa did upright in eyes of YHWH like David his ancestor.

familiar.text: And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, as did David his father.

modern.text: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אָסָ֛א הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּדָוִ֖ד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: He removed male cult personnel/consecrated persons from land and removed all idols his ancestors made.

familiar.text: And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

modern.text: He banished the male shrine prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר הַקְּדֵשִׁ֖ים מִן הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֨סַר֙ אֶת כָּל הַגִּלֻּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: He also removed Maacah his mother/queen mother from being queen mother because she made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it at wadi Kidron.

familiar.text: And also Maachah his mother, even her he removed from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa destroyed her idol, and burnt it by the brook Kidron.

modern.text: He also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole. Asa chopped down the pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

original.text: וְגַ֣ם אֶת מַעֲכָ֣ה אִמּ֗וֹ וַיְסִרֶ֨הָ֙ מִגְּבִירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר עָשְׂתָ֥ה מִפְלֶ֖צֶת לָאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וַיִּכְרֹ֤ת אָסָא֙ אֶת מִפְלַצְתָּ֔הּ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֖ף בְּנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: But high places were not removed. Nevertheless Asa's heart was whole with YHWH all his days.

familiar.text: But the high places were not removed: nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect with the LORD all his days.

modern.text: The high places were not removed, but Asa’s heart was fully devoted to the LORD all his days.

original.text: וְהַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא סָ֑רוּ רַ֣ק לְבַב אָסָ֗א הָיָ֥ה שָׁלֵ֛ם עִם יְהוָ֖ה כָּל יָמָֽיו

verses.restored: He brought into house of YHWH things his father dedicated and things he dedicated: silver, gold, and vessels.

familiar.text: And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated, and the things which himself had dedicated, into the house of the LORD, silver, and gold, and vessels.

modern.text: And he brought into the house of the LORD the silver and gold and other articles that he and his father had dedicated. War between Asa and Baasha (2 Chronicles 16:1–6)

original.text: וַיָּבֵא֙ אֶת קָדְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יו וקדשו בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה כֶּ֥סֶף וְזָהָ֖ב וְכֵלִֽים

verses.restored: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

familiar.text: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

modern.text: Now there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.

original.text: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֜ה בֵּ֣ין אָסָ֗א וּבֵ֛ין בַּעְשָׁ֥א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל יְמֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

familiar.text: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

modern.text: Baasha king of Israel went to war against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַל בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת הָרָמָ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֗י תֵּ֚ת יֹצֵ֣א וָבָ֔א לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Asa took all silver and gold remaining in treasures of house of YHWH and king's house and placed them in hand of his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram living in Damascus, saying:

familiar.text: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that were left in the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants: and king Asa sent them to Benhadad, the son of Tabrimon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

modern.text: So Asa withdrew all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace. He entrusted it to his servants and sent them with this message to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אָ֠סָא אֶת כָּל הַכֶּ֨סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֜ב הַֽנּוֹתָרִ֣ים בְּאוֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית מלך וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַד עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֞ם הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א אֶל בֶּן הֲ֠דַד בֶּן טַבְרִמֹּ֤ן בֶּן חֶזְיוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בְּדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: There is covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I sent you a gift of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he will go up from me.

familiar.text: There is a league between me and thee, and between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; come and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.

modern.text: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”

original.text: בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ בֵּ֥ין אָבִ֖י וּבֵ֣ין אָבִ֑יךָ הִנֵּה֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתִּֽי לְךָ֥ שֹׁ֨חַד֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֵ֣ךְ הָפֵ֗רָה אֶת בְּרִֽיתְךָ֙ אֶת בַּעְשָׁ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלָֽי

verses.restored: Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent commanders of armies against cities of Israel. He struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, all Chinneroth, and all land of Naphtali.

familiar.text: So Benhadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of the hosts which he had against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abelbethmaachah, and all Cinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.

modern.text: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and the whole land of Naphtali, including the region of Chinnereth.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע בֶּן הֲדַ֜ד אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר לוֹ֙ עַל עָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת עִיּ֣וֹן וְאֶת דָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת אָבֵ֣ל בֵּֽית מַעֲכָ֑ה וְאֵת֙ כָּל כִּנְר֔וֹת עַ֖ל כָּל אֶ֥רֶץ נַפְתָּלִֽי

verses.restored: When Baasha heard, he stopped building Ramah and lived in Tirzah.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard thereof, that he left off building of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.

modern.text: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ בַּעְשָׁ֔א וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל מִבְּנ֖וֹת אֶת הָֽרָמָ֑ה וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּתִרְצָֽה

verses.restored: King Asa summoned all Judah; none was exempt. They carried stones of Ramah and timber with which Baasha built, and King Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

familiar.text: Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none was exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.

modern.text: Then King Asa summoned all the men of Judah, with no exceptions, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials King Asa built up Geba of Benjamin, as well as Mizpah. Jehoshaphat Succeeds Asa (2 Chronicles 17:1–19)

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָסָ֜א הִשְׁמִ֤יעַ אֶת כָּל יְהוּדָה֙ אֵ֣ין נָקִ֔י וַיִּשְׂא֞וּ אֶת אַבְנֵ֤י הָֽרָמָה֙ וְאֶת עֵצֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּעְשָׁ֑א וַיִּ֤בֶן בָּם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֔א אֶת גֶּ֥בַע בִּנְיָמִ֖ן וְאֶת הַמִּצְפָּֽה

verses.restored: Rest of all acts of Asa, all his might, all he did, and cities he built—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah? Yet in time of his old age he became diseased in his feet.

familiar.text: The rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.

modern.text: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, along with all his might, all his accomplishments, and the cities he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? In his old age, however, he became diseased in his feet.

original.text: וְיֶ֣תֶר כָּל דִּבְרֵֽי אָ֠סָא וְכָל גְּב֨וּרָת֜וֹ וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה וְהֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה הֲלֹֽא הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה רַ֚ק לְעֵ֣ת זִקְנָת֔וֹ חָלָ֖ה אֶת רַגְלָֽיו

verses.restored: Asa lay with his ancestors and was buried with them in City of David his ancestor. Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place. Nadab Reigns in Israel

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אָסָא֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵר֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Nadab son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in second year of Asa king of Judah and reigned over Israel two years.

familiar.text: And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years.

modern.text: In the second year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel, and he reigned two years.

translation_notes: The summary that David never turned aside except in the matter of Uriah is royal idealization. The wider narrative records Bathsheba's coercion, census deaths, imperial violence, and household failures that must not be erased.

Maacah's precise genealogy and whether she is Asa's mother or grandmother/queen mother require audit. Her removal from office is political and religious action, not permission for misogyny or violence against older women.
Verse 12 again uses qadesh. It must not be translated or weaponized as a condemnation of LGBTQ identity; the historical reference is likely cultic personnel.
Religious reform does not authorize persecution, destruction of living communities' sacred property, forced conversion, or punishment of private belief.
Asa empties temple and palace treasuries to purchase Ben-hadad's betrayal of Baasha. Sacred wealth funds a proxy invasion whose victims live in northern cities.
Baasha's Ramah blockade restricts movement and economic life. Asa answers with foreign attack and then conscripts all Judah, with no exemption, to move construction materials.
Asa's foot disease in old age is a medical condition, not evidence of moral or spiritual failure.
Baasha's assassination of Nadab during siege and extermination of Jeroboam's entire house are coup violence and dynastic massacre. Prophetic fulfillment does not make collective killing ethical.
The narrative repeatedly says war continued all their days; ordinary communities bear the prolonged cost behind short royal summaries.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter against LGBTQ people, older women, disabled or ill people, or religious minorities. Do not sanctify proxy war, compulsory labor, assassination, or dynastic massacre through reform, prophecy, or idealized royal memory.
